curation.lead:
Chris Young is a Republican political consultant and former pharmaceutical trade association executive who, from August 2024 onward, simultaneously held three roles within or adjacent to the Musk organizational web: Director and Treasurer of America PAC (FEC C00879510), Vice President of United States of America Inc. (a Musk entity), and paid employee of Europa 100 LLC, a Texas limited liability company managed by Jared Birchall that was originally used to pay household staff and repurposed in 2024 to pay a political operative [Finding #4427] [Finding #5554]. His disclosed compensation from Europa 100 LLC ranged from $100,001 to $1,000,000 annually, with reporting indicating the actual figure was approximately $1 million per year [Finding #5785] [Finding #4458].

On January 30, 2025, Young was deployed to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau as a special governmental employee through the Department of Government Efficiency, gaining full access to CFPB data systems — including bank examination and enforcement records — by February 7 [Finding #4460]. During his CFPB tenure he appeared on internal emails discussing contract cancellations, penalty fund transfers, and mass layoffs [Finding #4460]. He also disclosed holding up to $15,000 in Amazon stock, a security on the CFPB's Prohibited Holdings list [Finding #4462]. Ethics experts cited by ProPublica assessed the dual-employment arrangement as a likely violation of 18 U.S.C. § 208, the federal criminal conflict-of-interest statute, because CFPB exercises regulatory jurisdiction over Tesla's auto-loan portfolio and X Corp's Visa payment partnership — both Musk enterprises that provide Young's income [Finding #4460].

Young's career before joining the Musk organization ran from field operations in Republican Party infrastructure — Nevada coordinator in 2012, Louisiana state director in 2014, RNC National Field Director from 2013 to 2017 — through a senior lobbying role at PhRMA, the pharmaceutical manufacturers' trade association, where he served as Deputy Vice President and then Vice President from 2020 to 2024 [Finding #4464]. PhRMA opposed Biden-era drug pricing reforms during his tenure there. He was hired by Musk in August 2024 to oversee America PAC, which received more than $239 million in direct contributions from Musk and spent $261 million in the 2024 cycle, including $78.8 million in in-kind transfers to United States of America Inc., the same entity where Young held a VP title [Finding #4427] [Finding #2637].

sections.title: Career Trajectory
sections.content:
Young's professional background is in Republican Party field operations and pharmaceutical trade association lobbying. He served as a field director for Bobby Jindal's 2007 governor's race, moved through state-level Republican National Committee roles in Nevada (2012) and Louisiana (2014), and reached the position of RNC National Field Director, which he held from 2013 through 2017 — a period spanning two national election cycles [Finding #4464]. He subsequently served as Executive Director of Engage Texas before joining PhRMA as Deputy Vice President, where he was elevated to Vice President by 2020, remaining until mid-2024 [Finding #4464]. At PhRMA, his tenure overlapped with the trade association's lobbying effort against the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug negotiation provisions.

In August 2024, Elon Musk hired Young to oversee America PAC operations. Salon reported the hire as a step to professionalize what had been a loosely organized political spending vehicle [Finding #4464]. Young was simultaneously installed as Director and Treasurer of America PAC (FEC C00879510), Vice President of United States of America Inc. (Musk as President, TX Comptroller TID 32097038932), and placed on Europa 100 LLC's payroll (TX Comptroller TID 32075024482, managed by Jared Birchall, PO Box 341886) [Finding #4427] [Finding #4458]. The Revolving Door Project documented the full career pipeline [Finding #4464].

sections.title: Financial Activity
sections.content:
Young's primary documented income source during the DOGE period was Europa 100 LLC, a Texas entity originally used to pay household staff for Musk before being repurposed in 2024 [Finding #5554]. His government financial disclosure reported income from Europa 100 in the range of $100,001 to $1,000,000 annually; ProPublica reporting based on that disclosure placed the figure at approximately $1 million per year [Finding #5785] [Finding #4458]. Jared Birchall is the manager of record for Europa 100, and Young also participated in an Excession LLC defined-contribution retirement plan — Excession LLC is another Musk entity — while serving as a CFPB special governmental employee [Finding #4458].

As Treasurer of America PAC, Young was the fiduciary of record for a committee that received more than $239 million in direct contributions from Musk and spent $261 million over the 2024 election cycle [Finding #3020]. America PAC directed $78.8 million in in-kind expenditures to United States of America Inc. — the same entity where Young held a VP title — creating a financial circuit in which the committee's largest in-kind recipient was also an organization whose officer was simultaneously the committee's treasurer [Finding #4427]. Young audited Blitz Canvassing tally sheets in Nevada, a vendor relationship that drew separate scrutiny; Blitz Canvassing is a GP3 LLC subsidiary that received $64.6 million from America PAC in 2024 [Finding #2637].

Young's government disclosure also identified up to $15,000 in Amazon stock, a holding the CFPB's own ethics rules designate as prohibited for bureau employees [Finding #4462]. A fellow DOGE aide at the CFPB, Gavin Kliger, separately held prohibited stocks — Tesla and Apple — valued at up to $715,000 [Finding #4462].

sections.title: CFPB Deployment and Conflict-of-Interest Questions
sections.content:
Young was deployed to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau on January 30, 2025, as a DOGE-affiliated special governmental employee, one of three Musk deputies added to the bureau's internal staff directory [Finding #5785]. He obtained full system access to CFPB data — including bank examination records and enforcement materials — by February 7, 2025 [Finding #4460]. Internal emails from February 11–12 showed him participating in discussions of contract cancellations, transfers from the CFPB's civil penalty fund, and workforce reduction-in-force planning; in March he separately inquired about RIF implementation [Finding #4460].

The structural conflict documented by reporting is that CFPB holds jurisdiction over Tesla's consumer auto-loan portfolio and over X Corp's January 28, 2025 Visa payment partnership — both Musk enterprises that are the ultimate source of Young's compensation through Europa 100 LLC [Finding #4460]. Ethics experts cited by ProPublica assessed this arrangement as one likely to violate 18 U.S.C. § 208 (criminal conflict-of-interest statute), which prohibits a federal employee from participating personally and substantially in a matter in which they hold a financial interest [Finding #4460].

Congressional oversight was initiated across multiple timelines. Senators Warren and Schiff wrote to the Office of Government Ethics and the CFPB Inspector General in February 2025 calling for investigation of Musk and DOGE officials [Finding #4465]. A second letter to the OGE followed on March 26, 2025 [Finding #4465]. On May 29, 2025, Senators Warren, Reed, and Wyden sent a letter to the Department of Justice urging a criminal investigation under 18 U.S.C. § 208 of DOGE employees at CFPB, with Young's arrangement as a central example [Finding #4465]. No public evidence of a formal subpoena directed to Young personally had been produced as of the investigation cutoff [Finding #4465].

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Elon Musk is Young's employer, PAC funder, and the ultimate source of Young's compensation through the Europa 100 LLC payroll chain. The relationship is documented across FEC filings (C00879510), Texas Comptroller franchise tax records for Europa 100 LLC (TID 32075024482), and the ProPublica disclosure investigation [Finding #4427] [Finding #4458] [Finding #2628]. Young reports to Musk organizationally through multiple concurrent entity relationships — America PAC, Europa 100, United States of America Inc. — each of which documents a distinct legal nexus to Musk's broader organizational structure [Finding #5554].

Jared Birchall is the manager of Europa 100 LLC, the entity through which Young is paid. Birchall manages multiple Musk Texas LLCs and functions as Musk's money manager and entity administrator. Young's compensation flows through Birchall-managed infrastructure [Finding #4458] [Finding #3018].

America PAC is the committee where Young held the Director and Treasurer title. The PAC spent $261 million in the 2024 cycle, with its largest in-kind outflows going to United States of America Inc. — where Young also held an officer title — and its vendor contracts including the Blitz Canvassing relationship that Young's own tally auditing work touched [Finding #2637] [Finding #3020].

open_questions: What specific bank examination or enforcement records did Young access during his CFPB tenure, and did any relate to Tesla's auto-loan portfolio or X Corp's payment operations? [Finding #4460]

What was the mechanism by which Europa 100 LLC — originally used to pay household staff — was repurposed to pay a political operative in 2024, and who approved that change in function? [Finding #5554]

Were Young's communications with CFPB staff regarding contract cancellations and workforce reductions conducted on government systems, personal devices, or Signal, as has been reported for other DOGE deployments? [Finding #4460]

Has the Department of Justice or Office of Government Ethics initiated any formal inquiry in response to the May 29, 2025 Warren-Reed-Wyden letter requesting a criminal investigation of CFPB DOGE employees? [Finding #4465]
What is the current status of Young's roles at America PAC and within the Musk entity web now that the formal DOGE SGE period has concluded?
